title: Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (2027)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary
This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's end-to-end procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contract intake and review, procurement lifecycle, and revenue recognition/billing controls. The document is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering managers who participate in financial planning or contract-related activities.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood business units globally.
- Covers fiscal planning cycles (annual budget and monthly rolling forecasts), vendor and customer contract intake and approval, procurement of goods/services, and revenue recognition for product offerings (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, and add-ons).

Definitions
- Owner: the budget or contract owner at Redwood who is responsible for execution and compliance.
- Spend Threshold: the dollar value above which additional approvals are required.
- RevRec: shorthand for revenue recognition.

Roles & Responsibilities
1. Finance (FP&A and Accounting)
   - Leads annual budgeting and maintains monthly rolling forecast.
   - Validates revenue recognition treatment and periodic close entries.
   - Maintains approval matrices and budget ownership mapping.
2. Legal
   - Reviews and approves customer and vendor contracts per playbook.
   - Maintains standard templates and clauses (IP, data residency, indemnities, SLA).
3. Procurement
   - Executes purchase orders (POs), vendor onboarding, and maintains vendor registry.
   - Ensures procurement controls and segregation of duties.
4. Product & Eng Managers
   - Own budget requests, forecast updates, and provide project cost estimates.
5. Revenue Operations / Billing
   - Implements billing configuration, invoices customers, and manages crediting/refunds.

Annual Budgeting & Rolling Forecasts
Overview
- Annual budget: top-down company targets aligned with the board-approved plan, typically finalized in December for the following fiscal year.
- Rolling forecast: a forward-looking 12-month forecast updated monthly to reflect actuals and expected changes.

Process (high level)
1. Planning kickoff (October) - FP&A issues guidance (headcount, opex baseline, growth targets).
2. Department submissions (November) - Owners submit line-item budgets via the budgeting template.
3. Review & iteration (Nov–Dec) - Finance and leadership reconcile and conduct trade-off sessions.
4. Board approval (December) - Final budget package and scenario analysis.
5. Monthly rolling forecast updates - Each cost center updates forecast with variance explanations by the 5th business day.

Budget Template (required fields)
| Line Item | Owner | Fiscal Year | Amount (USD) | Recurrence | Business Justification | Cost Center |
|-----------|-------|-------------|--------------|-----------|-------------------------|-------------|
| Headcount (Engineering) | Eng Manager | 2025 | 1,200,000 | Annual | New serving-runtime hires | ENG-SRV |

Approval Matrix and Spend Thresholds
- Up to $5,000: Department head approval.
- $5,001–$50,000: Cost center director + Finance.
- $50,001–$250,000: VP + Legal (if contract required) + Finance.
- > $250,000: CFO + General Counsel + Board notification (if multi-year or strategic).

Contract and Legal Intake Process
Purpose
Standardize intake for customer and vendor contracts to reduce legal risk and accelerate time-to-signature.

Steps
1. Intake & Triage
   - Requestor opens a contract request through the Contract Intake Form (Confluence link and ServiceNow request).
   - Intake fields: counterparty, contract type (customer/vendor), term, value, renewals, data residency needs, required SLAs, and termination clauses.
2. Initial Review (Legal triage within 3 business days)
   - Legal assigns risk tier (Low/Medium/High).
3. Negotiation & Redlines
   - Use standardized templates for low-risk vendor agreements and SaaS Master Services Agreement for customers.
   - Any deviation from the template must be documented in the Redline Summary.
4. Approvals
   - For contracts with revenue or spend above thresholds follow Approval Matrix.
   - Legal to confirm insurance/KYC requirements for vendors.
5. Signature & Storage
   - Use DocuSign for signatures.
   - Store final fully executed contracts in the contract repository (shared drive + metadata in Contract Management tool).

Contract Metadata (required for repository)
- counterparty_name
- contract_type
- effective_date
- expiration_date
- total_value_usd
- renewal_terms
- owner_name
- risk_tier
- confidentiality_level

Procurement Procedures
Procurement Channels
- Low-touch purchases (<= $5,000): departmental card or approved vendor catalog.
- Medium purchases ($5,001–$50,000): PO via Procurement team.
- High-value or strategic purchases (> $50,000): formal RFP and Procurement + Legal involvement.

Vendor Onboarding Requirements
- Completed vendor questionnaire, W-9 or equivalent, insurance certificates (if applicable), KYC checks, and assigned vendor ID.

PO Lifecycle (numbered steps)
1. Requestor creates Purchase Requisition with line-item detail and business justification.
2. Procurement validates vendor and adds PO term templates.
3. Finance confirms budget availability and issues PO.
4. Receiving team confirms delivery and closes PO in the ERP.
5. Accounts payable processes invoice against PO; three-way match required for invoices > $10,000.

Procurement Controls
- Segregation of duties: Requestor cannot approve their own PO.
- PO required for all non-card transactions above $2,000.
- Periodic vendor review: Procurement runs quarterly vendor performance and spend reports.

Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Overview
- Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606 (or IFRS 15 where applicable): identify contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate price, and recognize as obligations are satisfied.

Common Scenarios
1. Hosted API and Dedicated capacity (consumption-based)
   - Revenue recognized as services are delivered (usage-based recognition).
   - Monthly invoicing with meter data tied to backend usage logs.
2. Reserved/Dedicated capacity (prepaid commitments)
   - If customer prepays for committed capacity, recognize revenue ratably over the committed period unless distinct performance obligations suggest different timing.
3. Private deployment and professional services
   - Professional services: recognize based on percentage of completion or milestone method depending on contract terms.
   - Software license in on-prem bundle: evaluate the distinctness of license vs. services; recognize accordingly.

Billing & Invoice Policies
- Standard invoice cadence: monthly in arrears for consumption; upfront invoice for committed annual agreements with prorations handled at contract start/end.
- Required invoice metadata: customer_id, contract_id, invoice_period_start, invoice_period_end, line_items (product_code, quantity, unit_price), tax_amount, total_amount_usd.
- Disputes: customers must raise disputes within 30 days of invoice date. Credit memos issued after Finance approval.

Journal Entries & Controls
- Revenue deferral: upon receipt of prepayment, post to deferred revenue liability account and amortize per contract schedule.
- Cutoff controls: ensure all usage through the last day of period is included in period-end billing extracts.
- Monthly close checklist: billing reconciliations, deferred revenue rollforward, contract modifications review.

Audit & Compliance
- Quarterly internal reviews: Finance performs recon of billing system to recognized revenue.
- External audit: prepare contract sample sets, revenue schedules, and supporting meter logs.

Exceptions, Escalations & Dispute Resolution
- Escalate contract negotiation or procurement delays that block > $100k spend to VP of Finance.
- Billing disputes unresolved after 15 business days escalate to Head of Revenue Operations.

Operational Templates & Examples
1) Contract intake checklist (short)
- Counterparty legal name, tax ID, contract owner, risk tier, SLA required, data residency flag, renewal option.

2) Example PO line (CSV-friendly)
| sku | description | qty | unit_price_usd | account_code | cost_center |
| redwood-gpu-hours | Dedicated GPU hours | 1000 | 0.85 | 6100 | ENG-INFRA |

3) Example billing JSON snippet (for engineers integrating billing pipelines)
{
  "customer_id": "CUST-12345",
  "contract_id": "CTR-2025-098",
  "invoice_period_start": "2025-01-01",
  "invoice_period_end": "2025-01-31",
  "line_items": [
    {"product_code": "HOSTED-API-TOKENS", "quantity": "120000", "unit_price": "0.0005"}
  ],
  "total_amount_usd": "60.00"
}

Monitoring & Metrics
- Key FP&A and Billing KPIs: MRR, ARR, churn rate, days sales outstanding (DSO), deferred revenue balance, forecast accuracy (variance vs. actuals).
- Target metrics: DSO < 45 days, forecast accuracy within +/- 5% for operating expenses, billing disputes < 1% of billed revenue.
